text:
Parker Kelly is the kind of player the Avalanche keep finding: undrafted, built for the fourth line, and better than he looks. The Denver Post wrote about Colorado building another strong fourth line with him and Logan O'Connor, and he has three goals in 18 games at 13 minutes a night, including one in an overtime loss to Nashville.

The results are close to the process. His three goals came on 2.1 expected (the quality of his chances), and Colorado has 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, about even with the team. Evolving-Hockey noted his teammates were very strong last season, which flatters the raw numbers.

What made him valuable in 2025-26 was the other end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer chances with him on the ice than almost any forward in the league (98th percentile). He scored 21 goals last season, a surprise from a fourth-liner. Our projection sees about 16 goals this time, which would still be a fine return.
